title: Press Conference Ends with News of Son Found
seoTitle: Son found during live press conference in Florida
subtitle: Mother Thanks Sheriff and Citizen Who Located Benjamin After 48-Hour Search
excerpt: During a press conference in St. Johns County, Florida, Benjamin Adcock's mother received news that her 16-year-old son, missing for almost two days...
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A live-streamed press conference in St. Johns County, Florida, took an unexpected turn on Monday, September 14. As Olga Adcock made a public plea for help to find her 16-year-old son, Benjamin, who had been missing for about 48 hours, an off-camera voice announced that the teenager had been located.

Moment of Interruption

Olga was speaking alongside Sheriff Robert A. Hardwick of the St. Johns County Sheriff's Office when a woman attending the event shouted, “They found him!” The sheriff immediately turned to the mother and embraced her, as she repeatedly expressed gratitude and said there was light at the end of the tunnel.

How the Teenager Was Found

The official search apparatus included drones, helicopters, and K9 unit dogs, but none of these resources were responsible for the rescue. It was a citizen who, upon seeing a photo of Benjamin online, decided to call the sheriff's office and reported the young man's whereabouts.

Sheriff's Reaction and Promised Support

The microphone picked up part of the conversation between Sheriff Hardwick and the mother. Hardwick assured that the department would help better monitor Benjamin and that the corporation would cover the costs of this support. In a statement, he emphasized that the outcome was the best possible and praised the attentive citizen's actions.

Teenager's Diagnosis

Benjamin Adcock has a diagnosis of schizophrenia and mild autism, and is the eldest of five children. He had been missing for almost 48 hours when the press conference was held.

Conclusion of the Press Conference

The sequence of the plea for help, the unexpected announcement, and the embrace in front of the cameras marked the end of the two-day search, bringing relief to the family and reinforcing the importance of community collaboration in missing person cases.

With information from Extra online, SpaceMoney, Migalhas.
